pattern:
frost backs up your directories to Permafrost, S3-compatible storage, your
   own server over SSH or a local drive\. Everything is encrypted on this
   machine before it's uploaded\. Nobody else can read your files, not
   whoever stores them and not the frost authors\.
replacement:
frost backs up your directories to Permafrost, S3-compatible storage, your
   own SSH server, or a local drive. All data is encrypted locally before
   upload. Nobody else can read your files, including storage providers
   and the creators of frost.

pattern: this frost was built from source, so it can't update itself\. Rebuild it, or install a release with the installer: https://github\.com/([^\n]*?)#install
replacement: this frost build comes from source and cannot update itself. Rebuild from source or reinstall via the official package: https://github.com/$1#install

pattern: Nothing has changed since snapshot ([^\n]*?), saved ([^\n]*?), so there's nothing to back up\.
replacement: No changes detected since snapshot $1 (saved $2); nothing to back up.

pattern: Nothing has changed since snapshot ([^\n]*?), saved ([^\n]*?)\.
replacement: No changes detected since snapshot $1, saved $2.

pattern: all the words are real, but they don't make a valid phrase\. Check their order and spelling
replacement: all words are valid individually, but together they do not form a valid recovery phrase; check their order and spelling

pattern: scheduled job is missing, run `frost init` or `frost config set schedule\.enabled true`
replacement: scheduled job missing; run `frost init` or `frost config set schedule.enabled true`

pattern: Preview your first backup with frost backup --dry-run, or start it with frost backup\.
replacement: Preview your first backup using 'frost backup --dry-run', or begin the backup with 'frost backup'.

pattern: Run a new backup to re-upload anything missing, then `frost status --verify`\.
replacement: Run a new backup to upload missing data, followed by `frost status --verify`.

pattern: ([^\n]*?) didn't wait for you\. Save and close config\.toml, then press enter\.
replacement: $1 did not wait for editing to finish. Save and close config.toml, then press Enter.

pattern: Nobody can recover them for you: not whoever stores your backups, not us\.
replacement: Your storage provider and the developers cannot recover these words for you.

pattern: Make sure nobody's looking at your screen and you're not screen sharing\.
replacement: Ensure your screen is private and not being shared before proceeding.

pattern: They're the only way to restore your files if this machine is lost\.
replacement: This phrase is required to restore your files if this machine is lost or replaced.

pattern: back up this directory instead of the configured ones \(repeatable\)
replacement: back up the specified directory instead of configured directories (repeatable)

pattern: restore over the originals, replacing what's there \(asks first\)
replacement: restore and overwrite original files (asks first)

pattern: ([^\n]*?) was already set to that, but the job was missing\.
replacement: $1 was already set to this value, but the scheduled job was missing.

pattern: Anyone who sees this phrase can decrypt all of your backups\.
replacement: Anyone with access to this recovery phrase can decrypt your backups.

pattern: choose where to restore: --beside, --to <dir> or --overwrite
replacement: specify a restore destination using --beside, --to <dir>, or --overwrite

pattern: say which snapshot to restore, e\.g\. `frost restore latest`
replacement: specify the target snapshot to restore, e.g., `frost restore latest`

pattern: Write these 24 words down and keep them somewhere safe\.
replacement: Write down these 24 words and store them in a secure location.

pattern: show what would be uploaded without uploading anything
replacement: preview changes without transferring data

pattern: Set up frost: what to back up, where, and how often
replacement: Set up frost: choose what to back up, where to store it, and how often

pattern: Save your changes, then close ([^\n]*?) to carry on\.
replacement: Save your changes, then close $1 to continue.

pattern: also skip files matching this pattern \(repeatable\)
replacement: also exclude files matching this pattern (repeatable)

pattern: restore into a new folder next to the originals
replacement: restore files to a new directory alongside original files

pattern: restore into a new folder inside this directory
replacement: restore files to a new folder within the specified directory

pattern: Read or change settings without rerunning init
replacement: View or update configuration options without rerunning init

pattern: Everything in these files is already stored\.
replacement: All content in these files is already backed up.

pattern: list every snapshot, not just the latest 10
replacement: list all snapshots instead of only the 10 most recent

pattern: If one moved, update it with `frost init`\.
replacement: If a path has moved, update it by running `frost init`.

pattern: Press enter once you've written them down\.
replacement: Press Enter once you have saved them securely.

pattern: only say whether there's a newer release
replacement: check if a newer release is available

pattern: Run without --dry-run to back up\.
replacement: Run without the --dry-run flag to perform the backup.

pattern: To check: what's word #([^\n]*?)\?
replacement: Verification step: enter word #$1:

pattern: Where should backups go\?
replacement: Where would you like to store your backups?

pattern: (?<!\d)1 files kept changing while they were read, so the snapshot has their previous copy:
replacement: 1 file continued changing while being read, so the snapshot saved its previous version:

pattern: (\d+) files kept changing while they were read, so the snapshot has their previous copy:
replacement: $1 files continued changing while being read, so the snapshot saved their previous versions:

pattern: that's 1 words, a recovery phrase has 24
replacement: entered 1 word, but a recovery phrase must contain exactly 24 words

pattern: that's (\d+) words, a recovery phrase has 24
replacement: entered $1 words, but a recovery phrase must contain exactly 24 words

pattern: Run without ((?:\u001b\[[0-9;]*m)*--dry-run(?:\u001b\[[0-9;]*m)*) to back up\.
replacement: Run without the $1 flag to perform the backup.

pattern: And word #(\d+)\?
replacement: Enter word #$1:
